query: How can melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties be determined accurately and efficiently across the high-entropy-alloy family? State the physical rationale, expected quantitative performance, range of applicability, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive validation result that would rule out the proposed approach.

generation.hypothesis: Integrating high-throughput DSC with in situ high-temperature synchrotron XRD and atomistic free-energy simulations (under matched composition and temperature control conditions) yields accurate and efficient determinations of melting temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across a broad range of high-entropy alloy compositions.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloys prepared as well-mixed, single-phase or limited multiphase solid solutions with systematically varied compositions.
generation.intervention: Apply high-throughput DSC measurements combined with in situ high-temperature synchrotron XRD under inert atmospheres, paired with atomistic free-energy simulations that are calibrated to mirror the experimental heating rates and compositional variations.
generation.conditions: Experiments conducted over a wide composition range at controlled heating rates (using ambient or inert gas environments to avoid oxidation) with synchrotron XRD capturing phase transitions in real time, while simulations replicate these conditions to predict thermodynamic quantities.
generation.structural_mediator: The onset of melting and phase transformation as monitored by both DSC (heat flow anomalies) and real-time structural changes detected via XRD, which mediate the extraction of melting temperature, enthalpy/entropy of fusion, and volume change.
generation.mechanism: Precise control of experimental parameters (composition and temperature) allows for synchronized determination of phase change signatures (from XRD) and thermal events (from DSC). These signatures are directly incorporated into free-energy simulation frameworks to predict and refine liquid-phase thermodynamic properties, ensuring cross-validation between measurement and theory.
generation.predicted_outcome: The method will yield melting temperature and fusion thermodynamic quantities with quantitative accuracy typically within a 5–10% error margin, demonstrating consistency between experimental data and simulation predictions across the high-entropy-alloy family.
generation.baseline: Traditional single-composition, ex situ DSC or XRD analyses that lack the real-time, high-throughput coupling with simulations, often resulting in lower accuracy and limited compositional applicability.
generation.boundary: The approach is expected to perform well for high-entropy alloys with controllable oxidation and relatively simple phase evolution. Its accuracy might be compromised for alloys with rapid oxidation, extreme inhomogeneities, or very complex multi-phase behavior beyond the calibrated simulation range.
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainties remain regarding the impact of local microstructural inhomogeneities and potential minor oxide formation on DSC signal clarity and XRD resolution, which could affect the extraction of precise thermodynamic parameters in some compositions.

falsification_experiment.design: Select a representative set of high-entropy alloy compositions spanning the targeted range and subject each to the combined high-throughput DSC and in situ high-temperature synchrotron XRD analysis, while concurrently performing atomistic free-energy simulations under identical conditions. Compare the experimentally measured melting temperatures, fusion enthalpies, entropies, and volume changes with simulation outputs.
measurements: Onset temperatures of melting from DSC curves
Heat flow peaks corresponding to fusion events
Real-time phase evolution tracks from synchrotron XRD
Simulated free-energy profiles and predicted thermodynamic parameters
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If systematic discrepancies greater than approximately 15% (beyond expected error margins) are observed between the experimental measurements and simulation predictions across multiple compositions, then the integrated approach would be falsified.
